_readme: The Road Here (V1.7 build, October 2026; Phase 3A scaffold): every word on the page, section by section. **text** is set in bold (one phrase a paragraph at most); `accent` is the headline phrase in the accent color. No numbered eyebrows or chapter navigation (V1.7). Images are asset ids in assets.json (road-*). Privacy: the band is never named, linked or described in identifying detail anywhere on this page or in its metadata. V1.8: the milestone bar and the festival caption are removed; the hero portrait is a transparent cutout. V1.13: operator.groups carry a short label (the collapsed card) and a title that begins with it (the open card adds the rest), plus an icon (each card's large, faint, cropped graphic); each timeline milestone names its outline icon (Icon.astro). V1.14: school.board is the memorabilia board (RoadBoard.astro): John's three photographs (road-* assets), the two supplied logos, and the words on the designed artifacts (credential, touring map with the cities John toured, distribution and endorsement cards, setlist title). The map is a touring footprint, not an itinerary; the setlist lines are drawn illegible on purpose.

meta.title: The Road Here
meta.description: Before Web3, John Cowin spent over a decade turning an original music project into a professional touring business, and running the operations behind it.

hero.headline: Before Web3. There was music.
hero.copy: Before Web3, I spent **over a decade** turning an original music project into a professional touring business. What started behind a drum kit grew into an education in entrepreneurship, marketing, partnerships, creative work, and day-to-day operations.

school.headline: From practice rooms to 140+ shows a year.
paragraphs: I studied **performance, music business, and media**, then put that training to work building an original music project from the ground up.

What began with local shows grew into more than a decade as a professional musician. Along the way, I played major festivals, appeared on television and FM radio, earned an artist endorsement from an instrument brand, and secured **worldwide distribution through a Sony Music subsidiary**.

operator.headline: On stage at night. Running the business by day.
operator.copy: Before professional management and distribution came on board, I **handled much of the daily operation myself**. Even after the team grew, I **stayed close to the work** across touring, marketing, relationships, and live events.

pivot.headline: Then 2020 happened.
paragraphs: After years of near-constant touring, I was already ready for a life with more time at home. Then COVID brought live music to a stop.

Around the same time, I found DeFi. I studied the technology, joined projects as an investor and community member, and built relationships the same way I had in music: by showing up and contributing. That led to my **first professional role in Web3**.

timeline.what: Studied performance, music business, and media
Secured worldwide distribution through a Sony Music subsidiary
Began studying DeFi, investing, and joining communities
Started the first professional role in Web3

led.headline: Different industry. Same operating instincts.
led.copy: The context changed. The instincts did not. What I learned building audiences, relationships, and an operating rhythm on the road now shapes how I bring products to market.
